principle_text: When the persuadee responds with a personal question that diverts from the donation topic, avoid only polite acknowledgments and instead gently steer the conversation back to the charitable cause.
When the persuadee responds with neutral, casual conversation without showing donation interest, avoid focusing solely on small talk that does not guide the dialogue toward the charitable cause.
When the persuadee shows only mild recognition of a charity, avoid asking questions that do not clarify their understanding or move the conversation toward engagement.

When the persuadee shows initial interest or curiosity, you should connect the cause to familiar references and highlight specific impactful actions to engage their attention and encourage further inquiry.
When the persuadee shows openness and asks for more information, you should directly invite them to contribute to the cause to encourage engagement and positive commitment.
When a persuadee expresses openness to donating and past support for similar charities, you should be honest and transparent to build trust and encourage further engagement.
When the persuadee indicates they do not have children, avoid assuming personal connections to child-related causes without exploring other motivations.
When the persuadee indicates financial constraints but shows willingness to contribute in other ways, avoid focusing solely on monetary donations to prevent disengagement.
When the persuadee expresses curiosity about a charity's mission, avoid providing vague or unrelated information that does not directly address their question.
When the persuadee shows unfamiliarity with the charity, avoid assuming prior knowledge and instead provide clear, concise information about the organization's mission and activities.
When the persuadee expresses personal empathy, avoid shifting focus away from the specific charitable cause and its importance to the donation goal.
When the persuadee is responsive and positive, you should clearly introduce your charitable cause and directly ask for a donation to encourage immediate commitment.
When the persuadee responds positively to casual greetings, avoid focusing solely on rapport without gradually steering the conversation toward the donation purpose.
When the persuadee shifts the conversation to personal questions, avoid ignoring their curiosity and instead gently steer the dialogue back to the charitable cause.
When the persuadee shows limited knowledge about a charitable organization, you should introduce your personal connection and ask if they are familiar to engage their curiosity and openness.
When the persuadee shares personal information that does not relate to the donation goal, avoid only engaging in small talk without steering the conversation toward the charitable cause.
When the persuadee responds with friendly personal details, avoid focusing solely on casual conversation without steering the dialogue toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows openness to listen, you should respectfully request a moment to share information about the charity to engage their interest and build rapport.
When the persuadee shows general familiarity with nonprofits but no specific donation appeal has been made, avoid vague questions that do not directly connect to the charity or donation request.
When the persuadee shows openness to conversation, you should politely introduce the topic and ask for permission to engage, fostering a receptive atmosphere for donation discussions.
When the persuadee shares factual background without expressing emotional connection, avoid asking only informational questions that do not build empathy or link to the donation appeal.
When the persuadee is unfamiliar with a charity, you should introduce the organization to spark curiosity and encourage them to ask for more information.
When the persuadee expresses a positive personal connection to the topic, you should build on that connection to create emotional engagement and relate it to the charitable cause.
When a persuadee reveals past and current charitable activities, you should acknowledge their engagement and build on their previous support to encourage renewed or increased donations.
When the persuadee shows openness and empathy, you should share your own donation experience along with an emotional story to inspire positive attitudes toward giving.
When the persuadee is unfamiliar with the charity, you should introduce the organization clearly to engage their interest and open the door for further information.
When the persuadee shows polite engagement without clear interest in the donation, avoid using only neutral greetings that do not advance the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows curiosity and willingness to learn more, avoid giving overly basic or vague information that fails to engage or motivate them toward donation.
When the persuadee shows openness to engage, you should politely seek permission before introducing sensitive topics to foster trust and willingness to listen.

When the persuadee shares personal experiences of hardship with some stability, you should encourage empathy by connecting their story to the struggles of more vulnerable individuals to deepen emotional engagement.
